substantiveFindings: Verified all four input blobs at staging 7cdf8f42 and in the working tree (extraction 48,003 bytes). Pinned validators pass; the date receipt is hash-current, status research-blocked, with one blanket finding over all 71 items.
Read all 57 units (Music Officials and Eunuchs) in both English fields. Accepted repairs r0001-r0006 (s0042, s0044, s0048) are present in the source.

English: 14 definite field repairs across 8 units. Attribution: the empress dowager's rebuke (s0050) is addressed to Anren, not the emperor (s0044, s0049, s0052); the c0221 attribution is corrected to match. Mistranslations: 千秋萬歲後傳位 is succession after death, not abdication (s0016); 觀察使 is a Surveillance Commissioner, not a Military Commissioner (s0034, s0055); 涼陘 is Liangxing, not Liangjin (s0031); 巷伯 is in the Ya (Minor Odes), not the Greater Odes (s0026); and 萬卷 is ten thousand scrolls, not "thousands" (s0035). Inventions at s0020: "under Emperor Wen of Han" (the source names no emperor, and Prince Xiao's favor came under Emperor Jing) and the "Duke Zhuang's younger brother" gloss for 鄭叔段.

Identity: p011 (Emperor Wen of Han) and p012 (Duke Zhuang) have no Chinese mention or name; they exist only because of the s0020 English insertions. Both are removed with their claims and surfaces, and p013's link to p012 is cleared. No people are added, merged or canonically identified.

Chronology: 49 of 71 items verify as-is: correct era conversions or containing bounds (Hequ = AD 1044, Qingning, Tonghe, Kaitai 8 = 1019, early Chongxi 1032-1034, Shengzong's personal rule 1009-1031) and two true-unknown deaths that stay unresolved. 18 carry native changes and 4 disappear with the removed people. Seven attestations date figures who appear only in allusions, quotations or recalled examples (Jing Xinmo, Confucius, Huang Fanchuo, Tang Taizong, Prince Xiao of Liang, Shuduan of Zheng, Bo Diao). Five of them carry invented sourceDate text (English phrases, a book title, a name or a state). Under PEOPLE_DATE_AUDIT.md and the accepted jiuwudaishi/004 precedent they become undated attestations with empty hints. claim-53 gives Chongyuan the 1044 Hequ date of an episode he is absent from; it is replaced by the reign bound of the separate s0016 anecdote. claim-59 cites 統和, which is not in the unit, so its source witness is corrected and the interval is unchanged. claim-120 dated the Prince of Qin-Jin's death by Anren's 統和中 service; one-sided bounds of AD 983-1019 replace it.

Non-blocking observations, with no repair proposed. "Wang Jien" is the corpus-wide English convention for 王繼恩 (liaoshi/047, songshi/308; pinyin "Wang Ji'en" is retained in the record). The idiomatic s0042 label "Empress Dowager Qin'ai" anticipates her later status but is an identifying gloss for the posthumous title 欽哀 used by the source itself.

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 上嘗與太弟重元狎昵，宴酣，許以千秋萬歲後傳位。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: The emperor had grown overly familiar with his younger brother Chongyuan; deep in wine at a banquet, he promised to abdicate in his favor in the distant future.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: The emperor had grown overly familiar with his younger brother Chongyuan; deep in wine at a banquet, he promised that the throne would pass to him after his own death.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 千秋萬歲後傳位 is a euphemism for passing the throne on after the emperor's death. It is not abdication, which would mean giving up the throne while alive. The literal field already renders the euphemism correctly.

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 重元既恃梁孝王之寵，又多鄭叔段之過，朝臣無敢言者，道路以目。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: Chongyuan both relied on favor like Prince Xiao of Liang and committed faults like Duke Zhuang's younger brother Shuduan; court officials dared not speak, and people on the road exchanged glances in fear.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: Chongyuan both relied on favor like that of Prince Xiao of Liang and committed many faults like those of Shuduan of Zheng; court officials dared not speak, and people on the road exchanged glances in fear.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 鄭叔段 is "Shuduan of Zheng". The source does not name Duke Zhuang, so the literal field adds a person absent from the text (the extraction then created p012 from it), and it drops 多 ("many").

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 重元既恃梁孝王之寵，又多鄭叔段之過，朝臣無敢言者，道路以目。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: Chongyuan enjoyed favor comparable to Prince Xiao of Liang under Emperor Wen of Han and repeated the overreaching of Duke Zhuang's brother Shuduan; no minister dared remonstrate, and travelers only dared signal their alarm with their eyes.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: Chongyuan presumed on favor like that once shown to Prince Xiao of Liang and repeated the many transgressions of Shuduan of Zheng; no minister dared remonstrate, and travelers only dared signal their alarm with their eyes.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: The source names no emperor, and "under Emperor Wen of Han" is also historically wrong: Prince Xiao's celebrated favor came under his brother Emperor Jing. 恃 means to presume on. As in the literal field, Duke Zhuang is not in the source (鄭叔段 = Shuduan of Zheng). These insertions created the person records p011 and p012.

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 至巷伯詩列於《雅》，勃貂功著於晉，雖忠於所事，而非其職矣。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: By the time the Palace Steward ode was placed among the Greater Odes, and Bo Diao's achievements were celebrated in Jin, though loyal to those they served, this was no longer their proper office.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: By the time the Palace Steward ode was placed among the Ya odes, and Bo Diao's achievements were celebrated in Jin, though loyal to those they served, this was no longer their proper office.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 巷伯 belongs to the Xiaoya (Minor Odes) section of the Book of Odes. The source says only 列於《雅》 ("placed among the Ya"); "Greater Odes" (Daya) is a wrong section.

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 至巷伯詩列於《雅》，勃貂功著於晉，雖忠於所事，而非其職矣。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: Later the "Palace Steward" ode entered the Greater Odes, and Bo Diao won fame in Jin—loyal to their masters, perhaps, but already acting outside their proper charge.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: Later the "Palace Steward" ode was placed among the Ya odes, and Bo Diao won fame in Jin—loyal to their masters, perhaps, but already acting outside their proper charge.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: Same error as the literal field: 巷伯 is in the Minor Odes, and the source says only 《雅》.

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 初，皇后以公私所獲十歲已下兒容貌可觀者近百人，載赴涼陘，並使閹為豎，繼恩在焉。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: At first the empress took nearly a hundred children under ten years of age, of pleasing appearance, gained through public and private means, conveyed them to Liangjin, and had them all castrated to serve as attendants; Jien was among them.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: At first the empress took nearly a hundred children under ten years of age, of pleasing appearance, gained through public and private means, conveyed them to Liangxing, and had them all castrated to serve as attendants; Jien was among them.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 涼陘 is read Liángxíng (陘 xíng, a mountain pass), the Liao summer camp. "Liangjin" is not a reading of 陘.

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 初，皇后以公私所獲十歲已下兒容貌可觀者近百人，載赴涼陘，並使閹為豎，繼恩在焉。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: Earlier the empress had gathered nearly a hundred children under ten, handsome boys taken in raids and by other means, sent them to Liangjin, and had them all castrated as palace attendants; Jien was one of them.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: Earlier the empress had gathered nearly a hundred children under ten, handsome boys taken in raids and by other means, sent them to Liangxing, and had them all castrated as palace attendants; Jien was one of them.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 涼陘 is Liangxing, as in the literal repair.

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 聖宗親政，累遷尚衣庫使、左承宣、監門衛大將軍、靈州觀察使、內庫都提點。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: When Emperor Shengzong took personal rule, he was repeatedly promoted—to Director of the Imperial Wardrobe, Left Commissioner of Announcement, Grand General of the Gate Guards, Military Commissioner of Lingzhou, and Chief Intendant of the Inner Treasury.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: When Emperor Shengzong took personal rule, he was repeatedly promoted—to Director of the Imperial Wardrobe, Left Commissioner of Announcement, Grand General of the Gate Guards, Surveillance Commissioner of Lingzhou, and Chief Intendant of the Inner Treasury.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 觀察使 is a Surveillance Commissioner. "Military Commissioner" is the standard rendering of a different office, 節度使. The commentary at s0055 turns on exactly this title.

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 聖宗親政，累遷尚衣庫使、左承宣、監門衛大將軍、靈州觀察使、內庫都提點。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: After Emperor Shengzong assumed personal rule, Jien was promoted in succession to Director of the Imperial Wardrobe, Left Commissioner of Announcement, Grand General of the Gate Guards, Military Commissioner of Lingzhou, and Chief Intendant of the Inner Treasury.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: After Emperor Shengzong assumed personal rule, Jien was promoted in succession to Director of the Imperial Wardrobe, Left Commissioner of Announcement, Grand General of the Gate Guards, Surveillance Commissioner of Lingzhou, and Chief Intendant of the Inner Treasury.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 觀察使 is a Surveillance Commissioner, not a Military Commissioner (節度使).

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 繼恩好清談，不喜權利，每得賜賚，市書至萬卷，載以自隨，誦讀不倦。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: Jien loved scholarly talk and cared nothing for power or gain; whenever he received rewards he bought books by the thousands, carried them wherever he went, and read without cease.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: Jien loved scholarly talk and cared nothing for power or gain; whenever he received rewards he bought books until he had ten thousand scrolls, carried them wherever he went, and read without cease.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 市書至萬卷 means he bought books up to ten thousand scrolls. "By the thousands" understates the source figure by an order of magnitude; the literal field keeps "ten thousand scrolls".

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 會上思太后，親馭奉迎，太后責曰：「汝負萬死，我嘗營救。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: When the emperor came to miss the empress dowager and personally drove out to welcome her back, the empress dowager rebuked him: "You deserve ten thousand deaths; I once pleaded for your life.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: When the emperor came to miss the empress dowager and personally drove out to welcome her back, the empress dowager rebuked Anren: "You deserve ten thousand deaths; I once pleaded for your life.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: The rebuke 「汝負萬死，我嘗營救。不望汝報，何為離間我母子耶！」 is addressed to Zhao Anren. She had pleaded for his life when Rende wanted him executed (s0044), he had helped remove her (s0049), and s0052 records that Anren had no reply. "Him" after "the emperor" wrongly makes her son the addressee.

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 會上思太后，親馭奉迎，太后責曰：「汝負萬死，我嘗營救。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: When the emperor missed his mother and went in person to escort her back, the empress dowager reproached him: "You deserved death a thousand times over, yet I once saved your life.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: When the emperor missed his mother and went in person to escort her back, the empress dowager reproached Anren: "You deserved death a thousand times over, yet I once saved your life.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: Same attribution error as the literal field. The addressee is Anren (s0044, s0049, s0052), not the emperor.

definiteTranslationRepairs.chinese: 繼恩為內謁者，安仁為黃門令，似矣，何至溺於私愛，而授以觀察使、大將軍耶？
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: Jien as Inner Attendant and Anren as Yellow Gate Commandant would seem fitting enough—how could favoritism go so far as to grant them military commissioner and grand general?
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: Jien as Inner Attendant and Anren as Yellow Gate Commandant would seem fitting enough—how could favoritism go so far as to grant them surveillance commissioner and grand general?
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 觀察使 is a Surveillance Commissioner, matching the office Wang Jien received at s0034. It is not a Military Commissioner (節度使).

dateAuditReceipt.summary: Complete independent review of all 57 Chinese units, 71 date/hint checks, and 22 people. The chapter directly supports only the stated Qingning, Tonghe, Kaitai 8, and early Chongxi chronological contexts. Its undated 1044 military narrative, historical comparisons, and many active-date hints do not justify imported point dates, full reign spans, or lifetimes. These records are retained as source-specific research holds; no source or canonical extraction was changed.
